Deal_Headline: Les Laboratoires Servier Acquires Symphogen
Financial_Advisors: Lazard Inc , Rothschild & Co Bank AG
Legal_Advisors: Plesner , McDermott Will & Emery LLP , Perkins Coie LLP , Gorrissen Federspiel Advokatpartnerselskab
Description:
Les Laboratoires Servier SA, a pharmaceutical company, has completed the acquisition of Symphogen A/S, a therapeutic antibody discovery company.

Following the transaction, Symphogen will now function as the antibody center of excellence of Servier in several different therapeutic areas including oncology. Symphogen, now a subsidiary of Servier, will keep its operational autonomy and continue to rely on its experienced employees while maintaining its headquarters in Ballerup, Denmark.

As part of the acquisition, Christophe Thurieau, Executive Director of Servier Research Institute, has been appointed Chief Executive Officer of Symphogen and Karin Garre, former Chief Operating Officer of Symphogen, has been appointed General Manager of Symphogen. Martin Olin, former Chief Executive Officer of Symphogen, will act as an external consultant to support this transition.

This transaction enables Servier to strengthen its R&D pipeline by acquiring antibody pipeline and next-generation antibody technologies.

Lazard acted as financial advisor, while McDermott Will & Emery and Gorrissen Federspiel Advokatpartnerselskab acted as legal advisors to Servier. Rothschild & Co. acted as financial advisor and Plesner Advokatpartnerselskab and Perkins Coie LLP acted as legal advisors to Symphogen.

Deal History:

Announced: On April 3, 2020, Les Laboratoires Servier entered into a definitive agreement with the owners of Symphogen.
Deal_Rationale: This transaction enables Servier to strengthen its R&D pipeline by acquiring antibody pipeline and next-generation antibody technologies.

Deal_Headline: Pfizer Acquires Therachon for USD810 Million
Legal_Advisors: Cooley LLP , Homburger AG , Lenz & Staehelin , Arnold & Porter LLP
Description:
Pfizer Inc., a pharmaceutical company, has completion acquisition of all the shares of Therachon Holding AG, a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on rare diseases with assets in development for the treatment of achondroplasia and short bowel syndrome (SBS).

Under the terms of the transaction, Pfizer acquired Therachon for USD340 million with an additional USD470 million in additional payments contingent on the achievement of key milestones in the development and commercialization of TA-46. 

TA-46 is an investigational, soluble recombinant human fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) decoy, for bone development abnormalities associated with achondroplasia.

Prior to the closing of the transaction with Pfizer, Therachon will spin-off its apraglutide development program into a separate, independent company. Apraglutide is a GLP-2 analog in Phase II development for short bowel syndrome. Pfizer Ventures, the venture capital arm of Pfizer Inc., currently holds a minority stake and will continue to hold an equity stake in the new company.

The transaction is not expected to impact Pfizer’s current 2019 adjusted financial guidance.

The acquisition enables Pfizer to expand its rare disease portfolio with potential first-in-class therapy for achondroplasia through the development of TA-46.

Goldman Sachs acted as financial advisor while Cooley LLP and Homburger AG acted as legal advisors to Therachon. Arnold & Porter and Lenz & Staehelin acted as legal advisors to Pfizer.

Deal History:

Announced: On May 8, 2019, Pfizer entered into a definitive agreement to acquire all the shares of Therachon.
Deal_Rationale: The acquisition enables Pfizer to expand its rare disease portfolio with potential first-in-class therapy for achondroplasia through the development of TA-46.

Financial_Advisors: Rothschild & Co SCA , The Goldman Sachs Group Inc , Deutsche Bank AG , J.P. Morgan Cazenove Ltd (Inactive) , Barclays Wealth Management , Goldman Sachs International
Legal_Advisors: Shearman & Sterling LLP , Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP , Allen Overy Shearman Sterling LLP , Travers Smith LLP , White & Case LLP , Arnold & Porter Kaye Scholer LLP
Description:
Boston Scientific Corp, a medical technology, through its wholly-owned subsidiary, Bravo Bidco Ltd, has completed the acquisition of BTG plc,  a company which develops and commercializes products used in minimally-invasive procedures targeting cancer and vascular diseases, as well as acute care pharmaceuticals, for GBP3.3 billion.

In addition to the Interventional Medicine product lines, the BTG portfolio also includes a specialty pharmaceutical business comprised of acute care antidotes to treat overexposure to certain medications and toxins, and a licensing business that receives royalties related to BTG intellectual property and product license agreements.

Upon the effectiveness of the scheme of arrangement, BTG became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Boston Scientific, and BTG shares no longer trade on the London Stock Exchange. Under the terms of the previously announced transaction, holders of BTG common shares will receive 840 pence in cash per share. 

The transaction would be funded with a combination of cash on hand and proceeds from debt financing entered into by Boston Scientific.

The acquisition will enable Bravo Bidco to expand peripheral interventions portfolio with minimally-invasive treatments for cancers and vascular conditions.

Goldman Sachs International, Deutsche Bank AG, J.P. Morgan Cazenove and Rothschild & Co acted as financial advisors where as Allen & Overy LLP acted as legal adviser to BTG, while Barclays acted as financial advisor where as Shearman & Sterling LLP, Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP, Arnold & Porter Kaye Scholer LLP and Travers Smith LLP acted as legal advisors, respectively, to Bravo Bidco.

Deal History:

Announced: On November 20, 2018, Boston Scientific reached an agreement on the terms of a recommended cash offer by its wholly-owned subsidiary, Bravo Bidco Ltd, for the acquisition of the entire issued and to be issued ordinary share capital (100%) of BTG plc, a company which develops and commercializes products used in minimally-invasive procedures targeting cancer and vascular diseases, as well as acute care pharmaceuticals, for GBP3.3 billion.

Update: On December 12, 2018, BTG, Boston Scientific and Bidco entered into an amendment to the Co-operation Agreement to extend the date by which certain regulatory filings must be made in Spain, Germany and other relevant jurisdictions. The filing of the notification in respect of the Acquisition under the HSR Act was made yesterday.

Update: On February 15, 2019, The Transaction has received merger control clearance in Germany under the German Act Against Restraints of Competition and the Taiwan Fair Trade Commission has terminated its investigation. 

Update: On February 28, 2019, The shareholders of BTG have approved in respect of the previously announced recommended cash offer to acquire the entire issued and to be issued ordinary share capital of BTG by Bravo Bidco, an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Boston Scientific.

Update: On August 2, 2019, BTG and Boston Scientific are pleased to confirm that the Transaction has received merger control clearance from the US Federal Trade Commission under the HSR Act, on July 25, 2019 the CNMC issued a clearance decision under the Spanish Competition Act and on August 2, 2019, the Federal Competition Authority of Austria issued a clearance decision pursuant to Sec 11 Para 4 Austrian Cartel Act.
Deal_Rationale: The acquisition will enable Bravo Bidco to expand peripheral interventions portfolio with minimally-invasive treatments for cancers and vascular conditions.

Deal_Headline: Telix Pharma Acquires Atlab Pharma for USD10 Million
Description:
Telix Pharmaceuticals Limited, a clinical-stage biotechnology company, has completed the acquisition of Atlab Pharma SAS, a biotechnology company, for a purchase consideration of USD10 million.

Telix Pharma has exercised an option to acquire Atlab Pharma.  A total of 14,840,000 shares were issued in consideration. The consideration of USD10 million is issued as USD9 million in Telix shares to Atlab shareholders, at USD0.89 per share, USD0.5 million in Telix shares to BZL, also at USD0.89 per share. These shares are paid to BZL as partial consideration for a significant reduction in royalty rates for the background IP, as a closing condition of the transaction, and USD0.5 million in warrants over Telix shares to BZL, with an exercise price of USD1.34 per share.

As part of the transaction, Telix Pharma has also entered into a limited back - license with BZL Biologics LLC(BZL) for certain IP rights to support ongoing commercial research activities that are outside of the scope of product development focus for Telix Pharma. Prof. Jean-Francois Chatal (Atlab/ Universite de Nantes) and Prof. Neil Bander (BZL/ WCMC ) will continue to serve as members of Telix’s scientific advisory board.

The transaction enables Telix Pharma to support potential indication expansion for TLX591, notably the combination use of anti-PSMA therapeutics in conjunction with anti-androgen drugs, further increasing the value and relevance of its TLX591 program; Atlab Pharma possesses rights to an extensive clinical data set in approximately 200 patients that is highly informative to the development of TLX591, including unpublished data around dose optimization schemes for antibody-based PSMA radiopharmaceuticals. This data may accelerate and further de-risk the future development of TLX591; Atlab Pharma and BZL, together, bring considerable knowledge and expertise to the Telix team; and Atlab possesses the rights and materials necessary to develop huJ591, the most widely clinically-studied anti-PSMA antibody. Telix will keep huJ591 as a back-up clinical drug candidate and continue to support several high-value academic collaborations around the use of this antibody that may also be informative to the future development of TLX591, including in non-prostate cancer indications.

Deal_Headline: Sanofi Acquires Ablynx for USD4.85 Billion
Financial_Advisors: Morgan Stanley , Lazard Inc , J.P. Morgan Securities LLC
Legal_Advisors: Eubelius , Goodwin Procter LLP , Linklaters LLP , Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP , NautaDutilh NV
Description:
Sanofi, a pharmaceutical company, has acquired all outstanding shares of Ablynx NV, a biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of nanobodies, for an aggregate equity value of approximately EUR3.9 billion (USD4.85 billion). 

The Squeeze-out period commenced on May 22, 2018, in accordance with applicable Belgian and the US law, following the acquisition by Sanofi of over 95% of the outstanding shares of Ablynx upon settlement of the initial acceptance period of its tender offer for Ablynx. On June 12, 2018, upon expiration of the Squeeze-out period, 2,893,201 shares (including 7,163 shares represented by ADSs) and 8 convertible bonds of Ablynx were tendered in the Squeeze-out. The securities tendered during the Squeeze-out period are expected to be settled on or about June 19, 2018.

All shares (including all shares represented by ADSs) and all convertible bonds of Ablynx not tendered during the Squeeze-out are deemed transferred to Sanofi by operation of law. The funds required for the payment of the price thereof are kept with the Bank for official deposits (Deposito- en Consignatiekas / Caisse des depots et consignations). The former Ablynx holders of these Securities retain the right to receive EUR45 (USD55.92) per share (or ADS) and EUR393,700.78 per convertible bond. In order to receive these amounts, they must contact the bank for official deposits, where the funds will remain available.

On June 13, 2018, The shares of Ablynx were delisted from the regulated market of Euronext Brussels, (ii) the ADSs were delisted from NASDAQ Global Select Market and (iii) the convertible bonds were delisted from the open market Frankfurt MTF (Freiverkehr).

In accordance with the Belgian requirement of certainty of funds, Sanofi has entered into a bank credit facility, BNP Paribas Fortis SA/NA acting as the sole credit facility arranger. 

This transaction enables Sanofi to strengthen its R&D strategy with Nanobody technology platform and expands its rare blood disorders franchise with Ablynx’s late-stage investigational caplacizumab aTTP treatment. 

Morgan Stanley and Lazard Ltd. acted as financial advisors, Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP and NautaDutilh NV acted as legal advisors to Sanofi; J.P. Morgan Securities LLC acted as financial advisor, while Eubelius CVBA, Goodwin Procter LLP and Linklaters LLP acted as legal advisors to Ablynx for the transaction.

Deal History:

Update: On May 14, 2018, Sanofi and Ablynx  announced the results of the initial tender offer period of Sanofi’s previously announced tender offers to acquire all of the outstanding shares (including shares represented by American Depositary Shares (ADSs)), warrants and convertible bonds (together, the Securities) of Ablynx.

Update: On March 29, 2018, Sanofi entered into definitive agreement with Ablynx to acquire all of the outstanding ordinary shares of Ablynx at a price per share of EUR45 (USD55.92) in cash, which represents an aggregate equity value of approximately EUR3.9 billion (USD4.85). The transaction was unanimously approved by both the Sanofi and Ablynx boards of directors. Sanofi and Ablynx have received an approval and publication of the tender offer documents and response by Ablynx’s Board of Directors.

Sanofi confirmed that, as of the expiration of the initial acceptance period, which expired on May 4, 2018, a total of 71,972,994 shares (including 7,446,312 shares represented by ADSs), 2,594,841 warrants and 975 convertible bonds had been validly tendered into the offers and not withdrawn. Sanofi will own 95.60% of the outstanding shares of Ablynx on the settlement date of the offers, of which more than 90% were acquired through the offers. Sanofi further confirmed that the Minimum tender condition and the other conditions to the offers have been satisfied.

Under the terms of the agreement, Sanofi will commence the tender offers to acquire all of the outstanding shares (includes shares represented by ADS), warrants and convertible bonds of Ablynx in cash for  EUR45 (USD55.6) per share or ADS; EUR18.66 (USD23) - EUR41.79 (USD51.6) per warrant; and EUR0.39 (USD0.48) per convertible bond. Sanofi has complied with the formalities set forth in the Belgian takeover legislation and filed the mandatory documents with the FSMA.

Update: On March 27, 2018, Sanofi and Ablynx have received prospectus approved by the Belgian Financial Services and Markets Authority (FSMA).

Update: On March 1, 2018, Sanofi announced that the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976 has expired and that Sanofi has received clearance from the Federal Cartel Office of Germany in accordance with the Act Against Restraints of Competition, applicable to the transaction.

Earlier on January 5, 2018,  Ablynx rejected the proposal from Novo Nordisk A/S for up to EUR30.5 (USD36.2) per share, including EUR28 (USD33.23) per share in cash and one CVR with total potential cash payments over time of up to EUR2.5 (USD2.97) per share or total equity valuation of EUR2.6 billion (USD3.09 billion), taking into account the interests of all its stakeholders, unanimously concluded that the proposal fundamentally undervalues Ablynx and its strong prospects for continued growth and value creation.
Deal_Rationale: This transaction enables Sanofi to strengthen its R&D strategy with Nanobody technology platform and expands its rare blood disorders franchise with Ablynx’s late-stage investigational caplacizumab aTTP treatment.

Deal_Headline: Takeda Pharma Acquires TiGenix for USD626.4 Million
Financial_Advisors: Cowen and Company, LLC (Inactive) , Centerview Partners UK LLP
Legal_Advisors: Covington & Burling LLP , DLA Piper US LLP , Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP , DLA Piper UK LLP , Osborne Clarke N.V.
Description:
Takeda Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd., a pharmaceutical company, has completed the acquisition of TiGenix NV, a biopharmaceutical company developing stem cell therapies for serious medical conditions, for a purchase consideration of approximately EUR520 million (USD626.4 million). Takeda Pharma intends to fund the transaction cost from existing cash balances.

Pursuant to the transaction, TiGenix becomes a wholly owned subsidiary of Takeda.

On June 6, 2018, Takeda Pharma announced the results of the first acceptance period of Takeda’s previously announced tender offer in cash for all outstanding ordinary shares, warrants and American Depositary Shares (ADSs) and together with the ordinary shares and the warrants, the securities) of TiGenix that are not yet owned by Takeda and its affiliates, which expired as scheduled on May 31, 2018.

The second acceptance period for the Belgian offer will commence on June 20, 2018, and the second acceptance period for the US offer will commence today, June 6, 2018, and is scheduled to expire for both the Belgian offer and the US offer, subject to any extension, on July 3, 2018, respectively. The results of the second acceptance period are expected to be published on July 6, 2018. Payment for the ordinary shares, warrants and ADSs validly tendered and not withdrawn in the second acceptance period is currently expected to commence on July 10, 2018.

During the second acceptance period, holders of ordinary shares, warrants and ADSs can tender their securities in the bid by following the instructions set out in the prospectus or the tender offer statement on schedule TO, as applicable to them.

On April 25, 2018, Takeda Pharma announced that the first acceptance period of tender offer in cash for all outstanding ordinary shares. warrants and ADSs of TiGenix that are not yet owned by Takeda and its affiliates, at an acquisition price of EUR1.78 per ordinary share in cash; EUR35.60 (USD42.8) per ADS in cash and an amount per warrant in cash depending on the strike price and maturity of such Warrant, will commence on April 30, 2018.

The first acceptance period for the bid will start on April 30, 2018 and is scheduled to expire, subject to any extension, on May 31, 2018. The results of the first acceptance period are expected to be published on June 6, 2018. Payment for the ordinary shares, warrants and ADSs validly tendered and not withdrawn in the first acceptance period is currently scheduled for June 8, 2018 although the Belgian offer and the US offer may have different payment dates.

During the first acceptance period, holders of ordinary shares, warrants and ADSs can tender their securities in the bid by following the instructions set out in the prospectus or the tender offer statement on schedule TO, as applicable to them.

Pursuant to the transaction, Takeda Pharma intends to acquire 100% of the securities with voting rights or giving access to voting rights of TiGenix not already owned by Takeda Pharma or its affiliates at an acquisition price of EUR1.78 (USD2.14) per share in cash and an equivalent price per American Depositary Share (ADS), warrant and convertible bond, representing a transaction value of approximately EUR520 million (USD626.44 million) on a fully diluted basis. The transaction is structured as an all cash voluntary public takeover bid by Takeda Pharma with respect to 100% of the securities with voting rights or giving access to voting rights of TiGenix that are not already owned by Takeda Pharma or its affiliates. 

Takeda Pharma and TiGenix entered into an offer and support agreement confirming TiGenix’s support and the terms and conditions of the bid. Gri-Cel SA, holding 32,238,178 TiGenix shares, and its affiliate Grifols Worldwide Operations Ltd., holding 7,189,800 TiGenix shares in the form of ADS, have irrevocably confirmed that they will tender their shares and ADSs into the potential public takeover bid. 

The acquisition extends an existing exclusive ex-US license, development and commercialization agreement between Takeda and TiGenix to develop and commercialize Cx601 (darvadstrocel) entered in July 2016.

This acquisition enables Takeda Pharma to expand its late stage gastroenterology pipeline and strengthen presence in the US specialty care market.

Centerview Partners UK LLP acted as financial advisor, DLA Piper UK LLP and DLA Piper US LLP acted as legal advisor to Takeda Pharma; Cowen and Company, LLC acted as financial advisor, while Osborne Clarke CVBA and Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP acted as legal advisor to Tingenix for the transaction.

Deal History:

Announced: On January 5, 2018, Takeda Pharma intends to acquire TiGenix, for a purchase consideration of approximately EUR520 million (USD626.4 million). Takeda Pharma intends to fund the transaction cost from existing cash balances.

Takeda Pharma has also entered into an offer and support agreement with TiGenix which provides for a recommended potential voluntary public takeover bid for TiGenix. The agreement has been unanimously supported by the TiGenix board of directors (including its CEO).

The bid will be comprised of two separate offers (i) an offer to all holders of ordinary shares and warrants in accordance with the applicable law in Belgium (Belgian offer), and (ii) an offer to holders of ordinary shares who are resident in the US in accordance with applicable the US law and to holders of ADSs wherever located (the US offer).

Following closing of the potential voluntary public takeover bid, Takeda Pharma intends to launch a squeeze-out if the applicable conditions for such squeeze-out are met to delist the shares of TiGenix from Euronext Brussels and NASDAQ. After the squeeze-out, TiGenix would become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Takeda.
Deal_Rationale: This acquisition enables Takeda Pharma to expand its late stage gastroenterology pipeline and strengthen presence in the US specialty care market.

Deal_Headline: Cell Medica Acquires Catapult Therapy TCR from Cell Therapy Catapult
Description:
Cell Medica Ltd, a developer of cellular immunotherapy for the treatment of cancer, has acquired Catapult Therapy TCR Limited, a developer of cell therapy for the treatment of acute myeloid leukaemia, from Cell Therapy Catapult Ltd, (Cell and Gene Therapy Catapult), a developer of cell and gene therapies.

Catapult Therapy TCR is a company set up by Cell Therapy Catapult, University College London (UCL) Business and Imperial Innovations, and managed by Cell Therapy Catapult, for the development of the WT1 T cell receptor (TCR) cell therapy discovered through research at UCL and Imperial College London. The WT1-TCR cell therapy enhances the immune system to fight cancer by genetically engineering the patient’s T cells to target WT1, a tumour-associated antigen which is expressed in both solid tumours and blood cancers.

Concurrently, Cell Medica entered into a collaboration agreement with Cell Therapy Catapult, to establish cell therapy manufacturing operations for Cell Medica at the GMP production facility recently built by Cell Therapy Catapult in Stevenage, UK. The collaboration will include transferring the current WT1-TCR cell therapy manufacturing process to Stevenage over the next twelve months while Cell Medica and Cell Therapy Catapult work to develop a commercial scale production process using advanced manufacturing techniques. Cell Medica will also evaluate the feasibility of manufacturing additional cell therapy products at the site.

This transaction enables Cell Medica to create an effective treatment for patients with solid tumours.
Deal_Rationale: This transaction enables Cell Medica to create an effective treatment for patients with solid tumours.

Description:

Deal_Headline: Boston Scientific Acquires Symetis for USD435 Million
Legal_Advisors: Latham & Watkins LLP
Description:
Boston Scientific Corporation, a medical technology, has completed the acquisition Symetis SA, a medical technology company, for a purchase consideration of USD435 million in up-front cash.

The Symetis portfolio includes the ACURATE tA and ACURATE neo/TF valve systems for use in the treatment of high-risk patients suffering from severe and symptomatic aortic valve stenosis, which are sold in Europe and in other geographies outside of the United States. Symetis is also developing the ACURATE neo/AS next generation valve system, currently in a clinical trial intended to serve as the basis for a future CE mark application.

On an adjusted basis, the transaction is expected to be immaterial in 2017, slightly accretive in 2018, and increasingly accretive thereafter. The transaction is expected to be less accretive (or dilutive, as the case may be) on a GAAP basis, due to amortization expense and transaction and integration costs.

This transaction enables Boston Scientific to expand treatments for patients with aortic valvular heart disease and strengthen its position in structural heart globally.

Vischer AG acted as advisor to Symetis for the transaction.

Deal History:

Announced: On March 30, 2017, Boston Scientific entered into definitive agreement to acquire Symetis, for a purchase consideration of USD435 million in up-front cash.
Deal_Rationale: This transaction enables Boston Scientific to expand treatments for patients with aortic valvular heart disease and strengthen its position in structural heart globally.

Deal_Headline: BioLineRx Acquires Agalimmune
Legal_Advisors: King & Wood Mallesons LLP
Description:
BioLineRx Ltd., a biopharmaceutical company focused on oncology and immunology, has acquired Agalimmune Ltd., a developer of anti-cancer immunotherapy, and its technology platform for a initial consideration of USD5.85 million, of which USD2.85 million is in cash and the remainder in the Company’s ADSs. Additional consideration may be due to Agalimmune shareholders based on certain development and commercial milestones, including future sales of Agalimmune products. Deal_Headline: Cadila Pharma Sweden Acquires BioChromix NewCo
Description:
Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd, an India-based leading research-driven pharmaceutical companies, has announced the acquisition of Swedish BioChromix NewCo AB through its subsidiary Cadila Pharmaceuticals Sverige AB. The subsidiary has recently been established to investigate and facilitate business interactions between Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd and potential collaborators, academic groups, etc.

BioChromix NewCo AB develops new and innovative treatments against diseases involving misfolded proteins, which are believed to be central in the development of certain neurodegenerative diseases. BioChromix NewCo's unique substance class is believed to selectively bind to, neutralize and eliminate soluble, toxic protein oligomers, protofibrils and soluble aggregates that are believed to contribute to the neurodegenerative process in several diseases that affect the nervous system.

Cadila Pharmaceuticals will continue the preclinical and clinical development of the drug candidates developed by BioChromix NewCo. According to the agreement, development is to be based on milestones and will be carried out at Cadila Pharmaceuticals' state-of-the-art research facility in Ahmedabad, India. Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd. has all the resources necessary to take the project to the clinical phase and on to the market.

"The acquisition makes it possible to take the project, which was previously carried out by BioChromix NewCo, forward with significant resources. Cadila's expertise in drug development, together with BioChromix NewCo's scientific know-how in its field, provides an excellent platform for the further development of these unique drug candidates Provided that the development is successful, opportunities are created to enter into valuable commercial agreements in important geographic markets such as the USA and Europe," says Dr. Peter Åsberg, outgoing CEO of BioChromix NewCo under the proposed name change to CPL BCX PHARMA AB.

"There is a lot of promising research going on around the world, especially in Europe, which complements our research portfolio in pharmaceuticals. The acquisition of BioChromix NewCo, through our Swedish subsidiary, is a step towards establishing new domestic solutions at our own high-class facility for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases. This is an area of ??therapy that is of great importance to us," comments Dr. Rajiv I. Modi, Chairman and CEO of Cadila Pharmaceuticals.

"Going from the discovery electronic polymers interact with misfolded proteins in the university laboratory to medical innovation is a long step. The intellectual capital found in BioChromix NewCo was created through the transfer of university projects to the small development companies BioChromix AB and BioChromix Pharma AB. Cadila Pharmaceuticals' acquisition of BioChromix NewCo means that this knowledge is now transferred to an organization that can take the project to the clinic. I hope that it will ultimately lead to new treatments that can slow the progression of the disease and create a future benefit for patients suffering from these neurodegenerative diseases," says Olle Inganäs , one of the founders of BioChromix NewCo and professor at Linköping University.

Formerly BioChromix AB is part of UIC Alumni and has received advanced business development support through UIC's program UIC Business Accelerator .
Deal_Rationale: The acquisition of BioChromix NewCo, through Cadila's Swedish subsidiary, is a step towards establishing new domestic solutions at Cadila's own high-class facility for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.

Deal_Headline: Novavax Acquires Praha Vaccines
Legal_Advisors: Bird & Bird LLP , Ropes & Gray LLP
Description:
Novavax, Inc. a late-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation vaccines for serious infectious diseases, has acquired Praha Vaccines a.s., a manufacturing unit of Cyrus Poonawalla Group, in an all cash transaction of approximately USD167 million. 

The acquisition includes a biologics manufacturing facility and associated assets in Bohumil, Czech Republic. The facility is expected to provide an annual capacity of over 1 billion doses of antigen starting in 2021 for NVX-CoV2373, Novavax’ COVID-19 vaccine candidate. NVX-CoV2373 consists of a stable, prefusion protein antigen made using its proprietary nanoparticle technology and includes Novavax’ proprietary Matrix-M adjuvant.

The acquisition includes a 150,000-square foot state of the art vaccine and biologics manufacturing facility and other support buildings, along with the existing employees and all related and required infrastructure. The facility is completing a renovation that includes Biosafety Level-3 (BSL-3) capabilities. As part of the transaction, approximately 150 employees with significant experience in vaccine manufacturing and support have joined Novavax.

The acquisition of Praha Vaccines is supported by Novavax’ funding arrangement with the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), enabling Novavax to dramatically expand its manufacturing capacity. Novavax will work collaboratively with the Serum Institute of India (SII), part of the Cyrus Poonawalla Group, to increase production levels at the Bohumil facility by the end of 2020.

The transaction will allow Novavax to produce 1 billion doses of its COVID-19 vaccine candidate next year.
Deal_Rationale: The transaction will allow Novavax to produce 1 billion doses of its COVID-19 vaccine candidate next year.

Description:
Ascenion GmbH,  a technology transfer company with a life-science focus company and Innovationsstarter Fonds Hamburg GmbH, a financial service company acquire shares in PROVIREX Genome Editing Therapies GmbH, a biotech start-up.

The concept is based on research work by Prof. Joachim Hauber and team at the Heinrich Pette Institute (HPI) - Leibniz Institute for Experimental Virology and Prof. Frank Buchholz at the Technical University of Dresden, who was formerly at the Max Planck Institute for Molecular Cell Biology and genetics. Together they developed and optimized a so-called genetic scissors, the designer recombinase Brec1. The approach is currently being prepared for clinical trials in a cooperation between the HPI and the University Hospital Hamburg-Eppendorf (UKE). It will initially be evaluated as part of stem cell therapy in eight HIV patients in the UKE's Stem Cell Therapy Clinic under the direction of Prof. Nicolaus Kröger. For this purpose, the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF), the Hamburg Senate and ForTra gGmbH have provided funding and investment funds for research transfer to the Else Kröner-Fresenius Foundation.

Deal_Headline: Astellas Pharma Acquires Nanna Therapeutics
Description:
Astellas Pharma Inc., through its subsidiary Astellas Pharma Europe Ltd., has acquired all of the issued share capital of Nanna Therapeutics Limited, a biotech company focused on addressing age-related diseases with high unmet medical need including mitochondria-related diseases, through execution of a share purchase agreement.

Pursuant to the transaction, Astellas Pharma paid a consideration of GBP12 million upon closing of the acquisition, and Nanna became a wholly owned subsidiary of Astellas. In addition to this payment, Nanna’s shareholders are eligible to receive potential future development milestone payments of up to GBP57.5 million. The impact of this transaction on Astellas’ financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2021, is expected to be immaterial.

Adding Nanna’s proprietary and advanced screening platform with new DNA-encoded chemical libraries (DELs) technology significantly bolsters Astellas’ early stage drug development capabilities. Nanna’s unique capabilities enable the creation and rapid testing of more diverse chemical libraries. The approach enables phenotype-based screening which is not feasible with conventional DELs. It can also be applied to various assay systems including cell-based assays utilizing patient-derived cells, potentially enabling screens that are tailored to a specific disease biology.

The acquisition enables Astellas Pharma to create new solutions that address unmet medical needs by combining Nanna’s unique technology platform with its research and development capabilities related to mitochondrial diseases.
Deal_Rationale: The acquisition enables Astellas Pharma to create new solutions that address unmet medical needs by combining Nanna’s unique technology platform with its research and development capabilities related to mitochondrial diseases.

Description:
Klaria Pharma Holding AB, a developer of fast acting medicinal products that designs, develops and commercialize therapeutics for migraine and cancer related pain, has merged with Karessa Pharma Holding AB, engaged in research and development of novel drugs in male health and central nervous system therapy areas. 

The merged entity will maintain the company name Klaria Pharma Holding AB (publ) and will continue to have its registered office in Stockholm, Sweden.

The SCRO’s registration of the merger completes the merger process from a legal perspective and all of Karessa’s assets and liabilities have been transferred to Klaria. In connection with the registration of the merger, the SCRO has today registered the issue of 6,635,200 new shares in Klaria as merger consideration. Thus, Klaria has in total 38,728,448 outstanding shares.

As part of the transcation, new shares in Klaria will be issued to Karessa's shareholders in relation to their existing shareholdings in Karessa with the exchange rate 0.6032:1, i.e one share in Karessa entitles the holder to receive 0.6032 new shares in Klaria.

Based on the volume weighted average price during the last 60 trading days for Klaria's share, the offer values Karessa at approximately SEK4.47 per share, which means no discount or premium compared to Karessa's volume weighted average price during the last sixty trading days but a discount of about 25% compared to the closing price on November 4, 2019 of SEK5.95.

Shareholders in Klaria representing more than 37% of the votes and shares in Klaria and shareholders in Karessa representing more than 47% of the votes and shares in Karessa have committed or submitted their intention to vote to approve the merger at the forthcoming extraordinary general meeting.

Klaria shall pay merger consideration to Karessa's shareholders as set out below. When calculating the merger consideration, the Boards have only taken into account the volume-weighted average prices of the companies on Nasdaq First North Growth Market during the last 60 days of trading (as of November 4, 2019, the last day of trading prior to the disclosure of the merger).

One share in Karessa entitles the holder to receive 0.6032 new shares in Klaria, ie. new shares in Klaria will be issued to Karessa's shareholders in relation to their existing shareholdings in Karessa at an exchange rate of 0.6032:1. The shareholders of Karessa will thus receive an economic ownership of approximately 17.13% in New Klaria Pharma.

Furthermore, the Boards propose that the merger shall be implemented with Klaria as the absorbing company and Karessa as the absorbed company. All 11,000,000 shares in Karessa shall be included in the merger.

Only whole shares in Klaria will be paid to shareholders in Karessa as a merger Consideration. Klaria and Karessa will therefore retain a third party (Securities Broker) to aggregate all fractions of Karessa shares which do not entitle the holder to a whole new Klaria share and the total number of shares in Klaria corresponding to such fractions will then be sold by the Securities Broker at Nasdaq First North Growth Market. The sale will be made as soon as possible after the registration of the merger with the Swedish Companies Registration Office.

Avane AB as an independent financial advisor, while Setterwalls Advokatbyra acted as legal advisor to Klaria. Skarpa AB acted as an independent financial advisor, while Hamilton Advokatbyra Firm acted as legal advisor to Karessa.

The merger will create a drug development candidates based on innovative drug delivery systems with clear competitive advantages in each therapy area.

Deal_Headline: Canopy Growth Acquires Beckley Canopy Therapeutics
Description:
Canopy Growth Corporation, a Canada-based cannabis company, has acquired all outstanding shares in the global cannabinoid based research company Beckley Canopy Therapeutics (Beckley Canopy), including the joint commercial venture Spectrum Biomedical UK. These teams will now be integrated into the broader Spectrum Therapeutics organization to increase the breadth of the clinical research being pursued under the Spectrum banner and to combine continental European and United Kingdom commercial teams.

As a part of the acquisition, Canopy Growth’s European management structure will evolve. Paul Steckler and Steven Wooding will assume the roles of Co-Managing Directors in charge of all European operations. Paul is a seasoned pharmaceutical executive with over 20 years’ experience in commercial roles, having worked in both large and small pharmaceutical companies including Pfizer. Steve has held multiple positions within a 27-year career at Janssen, the Pharmaceutical arm of Johnson & Johnson. Most recently, he was head of Global Commercial Strategy and Market Access for Janssen.

“The acquisition comes at a time when commercial opportunities across Europe are ramping up,” said Mark Zekulin, CEO, Canopy Growth. “Spectrum Biomedical has completed all necessary approvals to import cannabis into the UK market and is proud to facilitate patient access to safe cannabinoid-based medicines there. Consolidating our UK-based operations will allow Canopy to simultaneously improve its research and commercial capabilities across the continent.”

Deal History: 

Announced: On August 9, 2019, Canopy Growth entered into an agreement to acquire Beckley Canopy Therapeutics.
Deal_Rationale: The acquisition of Beckley Canopy will allow Spectrum Therapeutics to continue expanding its medical cannabis leadership around the world, strengthening its foothold in the UK and more broadly across Europe.

Deal_Rationale: This acquisition will help strengthen NEC’s individualized immunotherapy programs.

Deal_Headline: Boehringer Ingelheim Acquires Amal Therapeutics

Description:
Boehringer Ingelheim International GmbH, a pharmaceutical company, announced its acquisition of all shares of AMAL Therapeutics SA, a biotechnology company focused on cancer immunotherapy and advancing therapeutic cancer vaccines derived from its technology platform KISIMA.

AMAL’s vaccine ATP128 is currently developed for stage IV colorectal cancer and is slated to begin trials later this month. Boehringer Ingelheim plans to develop new therapies by combining assets from its cancer immunology portfolio with AMAL’s proprietary KISIMA immunization platform.

The total transaction could amount up to EUR325 million, which includes USD225 million of upfront payment as well as contingent clinical, development and regulatory milestones plus up to EUR100 million if certain commercial milestones are hit.

This acquisition strengthens Boehringer Ingelheim’s strategic focus on immune cell-directed therapies.
Deal_Rationale: This acquisition strengthens Boehringer Ingelheim’s strategic focus on immune cell-directed therapies.

Deal_Headline: AbbVie Acquires Allergan
Financial_Advisors: Evercore Inc , The Goldman Sachs Group Inc , PJT Partners Inc , J.P. Morgan Securities LLC , Morgan Stanley  & Co LLC
Legal_Advisors: McCann FitzGerald , Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz , Arthur Cox , Baker & McKenzie LLP , Slaughter and May , Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP , Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP , Kirkland & Ellis LLP , Debevoise & Plimpton LLP
Description:
AbbVie Inc., a research-driven biopharmaceutical company, Acquirer Sub, a wholly-owned subsidiary of AbbVie, has completed its acquisition of Allergan plc, a pharmaceutical company, following receipt of regulatory approval from all government authorities required by the transaction agreement and approval by the Irish High Court. The transaction was unanimously approved by the AbbVie Board and the Independent Allergan Directors.

Under the terms of the agreement, Allergan shareholders will receive 0.8660 AbbVie shares and USD120.3 in cash for each Allergan share, for a total consideration of USD193.23 per Allergan share (based on the closing price of AbbVie's common stock of USD84.22 on May 7, 2020). Allergan common stock ceased trading on the New York Stock Exchange as of the close of trading today.

Pursuant to the acquisition, AbbVie shareholders own approximately 83% of AbbVie on a fully diluted basis and the Allergan shareholders own approximately 17% of AbbVie on a fully diluted basis.

The purchase consideration was based on the closing price of AbbVie's common stock of USD78.45 on June 24, 2019. The transaction represents a 45% premium to the closing price of Allergan's Shares on June 24, 2019.

Enterprise value for the transaction is USD85.74 billion.

AbbVie has secured fully underwritten financing commitments from Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. and MUFG Bank, Ltd., for an aggregate amount of USD38 billion, to finance together with AbbVie's own cash resources, the cash portion of the acquisition.

AbbVie's lead financial advisor, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC delivered a fairness opinion and has provided the committed financing for the transaction, and its legal advisors were Kirkland & Ellis LLP and McCann FitzGerald. PJT Partners LP served as a financial advisor to AbbVie. Allergan's exclusive financial advisor was J.P. Morgan Securities LLC and its legal advisors were Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and Arthur Cox. Weil Gotshal & Manges LLP acted as antitrust counsel. Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP represented Morgan Stanley and Debevoise & Plimpton LLP represented J.P. Morgan Securities.

Deal History:

Update: On May 5, 2020, AbbVie and Allergan announced that the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has accepted the proposed consent order in connection with the transaction. The acceptance by the FTC satisfies all required antitrust clearances needed to be obtained for the acquisition of Allergan by AbbVie. Further, AbbVie announced the extension of the expiration date of the offers to exchange any and all outstanding notes of certain series issued by Allergan Finance, LLC, Allergan, Inc., Allergan Sales, LLC and Allergan Funding SCS for new notes to be issued by AbbVie and the related consent solicitations being made by AbbVie on behalf of Allergan to adopt certain amendments to each of the indentures governing the Allergan notes. AbbVie hereby extends such expiration date from May 8, 2020 to May 12, 2020. AbbVie currently expects that there will be no further extensions of the Expiration Date.

Update: On April 28, 2020, Allergan has notified the NYSE of its intention to voluntarily withdraw from listing on the NYSE and from registration under Section 12(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended any and all outstanding notes and related guarantees issued by Allergan Funding following the consummation of the proposed acquisition by AbbVie by means of a scheme of arrangement. 

Update: On April 27, 2020, AbbVie announced the extension of the expiration date of the offers to exchange any and all outstanding notes of certain series issued by Allergan Finance, Allergan, Inc., Allergan Sales and Allergan Funding for new notes to be issued by AbbVie and the related consent solicitations being made by AbbVie on behalf of Allergan to adopt certain amendments to each of the indentures governing the Allergan notes. AbbVie hereby extends such expiration date from May 1, 2020 to May 8, 2020.

Update: On April 6, 2020, AbbVie has extended the expiration date of its (i) offers to exchange any and all outstanding notes of certain series issued by Allergan Finance, LLC, Allergan, Inc., Allergan Sales, LLC and Allergan Funding SCS for new notes to be issued by AbbVie and (ii) related consent solicitations being made by AbbVie on behalf of Allergan to adopt certain amendments to eliminate substantially all of the covenants, restrictive provisions, events of default and any guarantees of the related Allergan Notes in each of the indentures governing the Allergan Notes. AbbVie extended such expiration date from April 10, 2020 to April 24, 2020.

Update: On March 17, 2020, AbbVie and Allergan have entered into a consent decree agreement with staff of the US FTC regarding AbbVie's pending acquisition of Allergan. Under the terms of the agreement, AbbVie and Allergan agreed to divest brazikumab to AstraZeneca and Zenpep to Nestle. Nestle will also acquire Viokace, as part of the same transaction. The consent decree, including the proposed purchasers, remains subject to further review and approval by the Commissioners of the FTC. The transaction is being pushed back to at least May after the US Justice Department said it will delay merger and acquisition reviews because of interruptions caused by the coronavirus pandemic. 

Update: On March 3, 2020, AbbVie and Allergan, announced that the European Commission has approved the divestiture of brazikumab to AstraZeneca. The European Commission's approval of AbbVie's pending acquisition of Allergan in January was conditional upon the divestiture of brazikumab to a suitable purchaser. The transaction remains subject to additional customary closing conditions, but the European Commission's final approval clears the pathway in Europe to close the pending transaction.

Update: On February 24, 2020, AbbVie announced the extension of the expiration date of the offers to exchange any and all outstanding notes of certain series issued by AbbVie and the related consent solicitations being made by AbbVie. AbbVie hereby extends such expiration date from 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on February 28, 2020 to 5:00 p.m., on March 13, 2020.

Update: On February 18, 2020, Coalition of consumer groups and unions hopes to convince the FTC to alter the terms of AbbVie’s (ABBV) USD63 billion acquisition of Allergan by arguing the deal as currently conceived would thwart competition and unfairly maintain higher drug prices for consumers.

Update: On January 10, 2020, AbbVie and Allergan received conditional approval of the transaction by the European Commission, subject to the approved divestiture of brazikumab and other conditions.

Update: On January 8, 2020, AbbVie announced the creation of a new global business, Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, and the proposed leadership team for the combined company, effective upon the expected first-quarter 2020 close of the Allergan acquisition.

Update: On October 14, 2019, Allergan's shareholders have voted to approve the proposed acquisition of Allergan by AbbVie. More than 99% of the votes cast at both a special court-ordered meeting of shareholders and at an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders were in favor of the transaction, representing approximately 68.6% of the shares outstanding and eligible to be voted.

Update: On September 27, 2019, AbbVie and Allergan have each received a Request for Additional Information (Second Request) from the FTC in connection with AbbVie's pending acquisition of Allergan.

Announced: On June 25, 2019, AbbVie, Acquirer Sub, a wholly-owned subsidiary of AbbVie, and Allergan plc, entered into a definitive transaction agreement under which AbbVie agreed to acquire Allergan in a cash and stock transaction for a transaction equity value of approximately USD63 billion.
Deal_Rationale: This acquisition enables Abbvie, new growth platforms and positions to diversify and expand its revenue base; scale and enhanced profitability for its's growth platform.

Deal_Headline: PerkinElmer Acquires Cisbio Bioassays
Legal_Advisors: Taylor Wessing LLP , DLA Piper LLP (US) , Hogan Lovells International LLP
Description:
PerkinElmer, Inc., a provider of products, services, and solutions to the diagnostics, life sciences, and applied services markets, has acquired Cisbio Bioassays, a custom assay service provider, from Abenex Capital.

Founded in 1974, and headquartered in Codolet, France, Cisbio develops, manufactures and markets high quality kits and reagents for the life sciences and diagnostics markets. 

The acquisition will expand PerkinElmer’s current offerings for life sciences researchers, which include a wide range of validated drug discovery screening reagents and kits for high throughput and profiling assays, as well as research-use only in vitro diagnostic kits. Specifically, Cisbio’s market-leading HTRF screening technology can be integrated into PerkinElmer’s customers’ upstream workflows such as target identification and characterization, along with downstream applications such as lead optimization and validation. Cisbio also significantly expands PerkinElmer’s cell-based assay R&D capabilities, and from a commercial standpoint, PerkinElmer expects to be able to leverage Cisbio’s customer base in growth regions including the Americas, Europe and China to expand its market reach for reagents.

This acquisition bolsters PerkinElmer’s position in life sciences and diagnostics markets. 

Hogan Lovells acted as legal advisor to PerkinElmer. Edmond de Rothschild acted as financial advisor and DLA Piper and Taylor Wessing acted as legal advisor to Abenex.
Deal_Rationale: This acquisition bolsters PerkinElmer’s position in life sciences and diagnostics markets.

Deal_Headline: Hansa Biopharma Divests its Equity Stake in Genovis
Description:
Hansa Biopharma AB, a company engaged in immunomodulatory enzyme technology for rare IgG-mediated diseases, has divested its entire equity stake in Genovis AB. The transaction generated gross proceeds of SEK89 million (USD9.59 million).

The placing of 5.7 million shares in Genovis, which amounts to 9% of the issued share capital in the Company, was completed on April 12, 2019. The transaction generated proceeds before tax of SEK89 million, based on a Genovis share price of SEK15.64. Hansa acquired the shares at an average share price of SEK2.19 per Genovis share.

Genovis is a company engaged in the development of enzymatic research tools and technologies, applied in e.g. development and quality control of antibody-based drugs. Primarily in 2011, Hansa Biopharma made a strategic and financial investment in Genovis.

Hansa Biopharma intends to use the proceeds for working capital not only to expedite further the clinical development program of imlifidase in transplant rejection and autoimmune diseases, but also to ramp up preparations for clinical studies with the recently selected lead in the NiceR-program, Hansas program for development of novel IgG-cleaving enzymes for repeat dosing.

Cord Communications is acting as advisor for Swedish Investor and Media Relations; FTI Consulting for U.K. Investor and Media Relations; Argot Partners for U.S. Investor and Media Relations to Hansa Biopharma for the transaction.
Deal_Rationale: Hansa Biopharma intends to use the proceeds for working capital not only to expedite further the clinical development program of imlifidase in transplant rejection and autoimmune diseases, but also to ramp up preparations for clinical studies with the recently selected lead in the NiceR-program, Hansas program for development of novel IgG-cleaving enzymes for repeat dosing.

Description:
Boehringer Ingelheim GmbH, a research-driven pharmaceutical company, has acquired ICD Therapeutics GmbH. The acquisition includes rights to ICD’s MacroDel biologics-delivery platform.

Deal_Headline: Pfizer Acquires 15% Stake in Vivet Therapeutics for USD51 Million
Description:
Vivet Therapeutics, a privately held gene therapy biotech company dedicated to developing gene therapy treatments for inherited liver disorder, and Pfizer Inc., announced that Pfizer has acquired a 15% equity interest in Vivet and secured an exclusive option to acquire all outstanding shares.

Pfizer and Vivet will collaborate on the development of VTX-801, Vivet’s proprietary treatment for Wilson disease.

Under the terms of the transaction, Pfizer paid approximately EUR45 million (USD51.09 million) upon signing and may pay up to EUR560 million (USD635.82 million) inclusive of the option exercise payment and subject to certain clinical, regulatory, and commercial milestones. Pfizer can exercise its option to acquire 100% of Vivet following the company’s delivery of certain data from the Phase I/II clinical trial for VTX-801. As part of the transaction, Pfizer senior executive Monika Vnuk, vice president, Worldwide Business Development, will join Vivet’s Board of Directors.

This transaction will help accelerate development of VTX-801 and expand other innovative technologies.
Deal_Rationale: This transaction will help accelerate development of VTX-801 and expand other innovative technologies.

Deal_Headline: Biogen Acquires Nightstar Therapeutics
Financial_Advisors: Centerview Partners LLC , Jefferies LLC , Goldman Sachs & Co LLC
Legal_Advisors: Sullivan & Cromwell LLP , Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP & Affiliates , Ropes & Gray LLP , Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson LLP , Finsbury - UK (Inactive)
Description:
Biogen Inc., a discovers, develops and delivers therapies for people living with serious neurological and neurodegenerative diseases, has completed the acquisition of Nightstar Therapeutics plc (NST), a clinical-stage gene therapy company, which is focused on adeno-associated virus (AAV) treatments for inherited retinal disorders, for USD25.5 per share in cash. 

As a result of the acquisition, Biogen now has added two mid- to late-stage clinical assets, as well as preclinical programs, in ophthalmology. 

Pursuant to acquisition, Nightstar Therapeutics and Biogen have reached agreement on the terms of a recommended acquisition whereby the entire issued and to be issued share capital of Nightstar will be acquired by Tungsten Bidco Limited (a newly-incorporated company and wholly-owned subsidiary of Biogen Switzerland Holdings GmhH (Bidder)). It is intended that the proposed acquisition will be implemented by means of a U.K. Court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement under Part 26 of the U.K. Companies Act 2006.

Under the terms of the acquisition, Nightstar Shareholders will be entitled to receive USD25.50 in cash for each Nightstar Share. The terms of the Acquisition values Nightstar’s entire issued and to be issued share capital at approximately USD877 million and the terms of the Acquisition represent a premium of approximately 70%.

This acquisition enables Biogen to establish clinical pipeline of gene therapy candidates in ophthalmology.

Goldman, Sachs & Co. acted as financial advisor and Ropes & Gray LLP acted as legal advisor to Biogen. Centerview Partners acted as financial advisor and Finsbury acted as PR adviser and Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP acted as legal advisor to NST for the transaction.

Deal History:

Update: On May 8, 2019, Nightstar Therapeutics announced at the general meeting and the court meeting held earlier today in connection with the recommended acquisition of the entire issued and to be issued share capital of Nightstar by Tungsten Bidco Limited, a newly-incorporated company and wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Biogen, all resolutions proposed were passed by the requisite majorities and accordingly the scheme was approved.

Update: On April 26, 2019, Nightstar Therapeutics announced that both independent proxy advisory firms, Institutional Shareholder Services and Glass Lewis & Co. have recommended that Nightstar shareholders vote for the proposals relating to the proposed acquisition of Nightstar by an affiliate of Biogen.

Announced: On March 4, 2019, Biogen agreed to acquire NST, which is focused on adeno-associated virus (AAV) treatments for inherited retinal disorders, for USD25.5 per share in cash. The acquisition of NST is planned to be funded through available cash and accounted for as an acquisition of a business. Biogen expects to complete the acquisition by mid-year 2019.
Deal_Rationale: This acquisition enables Biogen to establish clinical pipeline of gene therapy candidates in ophthalmology.

Deal_Headline: Charles River Labs Acquires Citoxlab for USD510 Million
Legal_Advisors: Axinn, Veltrop & Harkrider LLP , Goodwin Procter LLP , Darrois Villey Maillot Brochier A.A.R.P.I.
Description:
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc., has completed the acquisition of Citoxlab Group, for EUR448 million (USD510 million) in cash, subject to customary closing adjustments. The proposed acquisition and associated fees are expected to be financed through Charles River’s existing revolving credit facility and cash.

Citoxlab is a non-clinical contract research organization (CRO), specializing in regulated safety assessment services, non-regulated discovery services, and medical device testing. 

The purchase price implies multiples of 13.8x non-GAAP EBITDA based on Citoxlab’s estimated last twelve-month results prior to the anticipated close, and approximately 11.7x non-GAAP EBITDA based on the estimated forward twelve-month results after the anticipated close.

The acquisition will enable Charles River to further strengthen its position as CRO by expanding its scientific portfolio and geographic footprint, which would enhance its ability to partner with clients across the drug discovery and development continuum.

The proposed acquisition is expected to add USD115 to USD130 million to Charles River’s 2019 consolidated revenue based on the anticipated second-quarter close and approximately USD200 million to 2020 consolidated revenue. Citoxlab’s revenue is expected to grow at a high-single-digit rate, which is consistent with the long-term organic revenue growth target for Charles River’s Discovery and Safety Assessment (DSA) segment. Citoxlab is expected to be reported as part of Charles River’s DSA segment.

The proposed transaction is expected to be accretive to non-GAAP earnings per share by approximately USD0.15 in 2019 and at least USD0.35 in 2020. Items excluded from non-GAAP earnings per share are expected to include all acquisition-related costs, which primarily include amortization of intangible assets, advisory fees, and integration costs.

Evercore Inc., (formerly Evercore Partners) acted as the exclusive financial advisor to Charles River. Darrois Villey Maillot Brochier acted as Charles River’s transactional legal counsel and Axinn, Veltrop & Harkrider LLP acted as antitrust counsel. Goodwin Procter LLP acted as Citoxlab’s transactional legal counsel.

Deal History:

Announced: On February 13, 2019, Charles River Laboratories signed a binding offer to acquire Citoxlab, for EUR448 million (USD510 million) in cash, subject to customary closing adjustments. The proposed acquisition and associated fees are expected to be financed through Charles River’s existing revolving credit facility and cash.
Deal_Rationale: The acquisition of will enable Charles River to further strengthen its position as CRO by expanding its scientific portfolio and geographic footprint, which would enhance its ability to partner with clients across the drug discovery and development continuum.

Deal_Headline: Neuraxpharm Acquires Farmax from SVUS Pharma
Description:
Neuraxpharm Group, a pharmaceutical company focused on the treatment of central nervous system disorders (CNS), has acquired Farmax, a CNS specialty pharmaceutical company, from SVUS Pharma, a contract pharmaceutical manufacturing company.

Farmax, located in Czech Republic, was the commercial division of SVUS Pharma, and has a distribution presence in the Czech Republic, Slovakia as well as a small presence in Hungary. Farmax is engaged in sales and marketing both branded and non-branded generics pharmaceuticals for CNS disorders such as Zolpinox. It also commercializes well-known OTC nutraceuticals such as Preventan and Maxicor.

Following the transaction, Farmax has been renamed Neuraxpharm Bohemia s.r.o. and will commercialize its products under the Neuraxpharm brand. Leveraging its proprietary sales force in the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Hungary, Neuraxpharm Bohemia plans to quickly offer new and differentiated products to local patients and healthcare providers based on the group’s broad CNS portfolio.

This transaction enables Neuraxpharm to expand its pan-European footprint in Central and Eastern Europe.
Deal_Rationale: This transaction enables Neuraxpharm to expand its pan-European footprint in Central and Eastern Europe.

Description:
Hitachi Chemical Advanced Therapeutics Solutions, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Hitachi Chemical Company, Ltd., has completed the acquisition of apceth Biopharma GmbH, a company engaged in development and manufacturing of cell-based and gene therapy products, from apceth GmbH & Co. KG, a biopharmaceutical company, for a purchase consideration of approximately EUR75.5 million (USD86.38 million).

Through this deal, Hitachi Chemical will acquire two state-of-the-art GMP/BSL2 production facilities including 600 m2 of cleanroom area.

Utilizing apceth Biopharma’s manufacturing sites as well as its wide range of sales network, Hitachi Chemical Group will expand its regenerative medicine business further. The Group will also work to construct a framework that assures timely manufacture and shipment of uniform quality products in each region to its customers of the pharmaceutical manufacturers who sell their products globally, by combining the manufacturing know-how that Hitachi Chemical Group has acquired in line with the US and Japanese regulations in relation to regenerative medicine products with the know-how that apceth Biopharma has acquired in accordance with European regulations.

This acquisition allows Hitachi Chemical to construct a framework of manufacturing regenerative medicine products in the US, Japan, and Europe.

GCA Altium Limited acted as financial advisor and Baker McKenzie acted as legal advisor to Hitachi Chemical for the transaction.

Deal History: 

Announced: On January 31, 2019, Hitachi Chemical has agreed to acquire all the stock of apceth Biopharma from apceth GmbH, for a purchase consideration of approximately EUR75.5 million (USD86.38 million).
Deal_Rationale: This acquisition allows Hitachi Chemical to construct a framework of manufacturing regenerative medicine products in the US, Japan, and Europe.

Deal_Headline: Vital Therapies Acquires Immunic
Financial_Advisors: BMO Capital Markets Corp , Ladenburg Thalmann & Co Inc
Legal_Advisors: Dentons UK and Middle East LLP , Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman LLP
Description:
Vital Therapies, Inc., a biotherapeutic company, has acquired all of the outstanding shares in and Immunic AG, a clinical-stage biotechnology company, in exchange for newly issued shares in an all-stock transaction.

The company has been renamed Immunic, Inc. and its common stock is expected to commence trading on The NASDAQ Capital Market under the ticker symbol 'IMUX' on April 15, 2019. 

Under the terms of the agreement, on a pro forma basis and after giving effect to the concurrent financing, current Vital Therapies stockholders are expected to own approximately 11% of the company and current Immunic stockholders are expected to own approximately 89% of the company. The actual allocation will be subject to adjustment based on Vital Therapies’ net cash balance at the closing of the transaction. Prior to closing, Vital Therapies will seek stockholder approval to effect a reverse split of its outstanding common stock to satisfy listing requirements of the NASDAQ global market. Vital Therapies will focus on advancing Immunic‘s pipeline of novel and potentially transformative treatments for chronic inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.  Upon closing of the transaction, Vital Therapies is expected to operate under the name Immunic, Inc. and trade on the NASDAQ global market.

The company will be led by Daniel Vitt, CEO and president of Immunic, and will be headquartered in Boston, MA, US. The board of directors is expected to be composed of five members, including four members of the current Immunic board, Daniel Vitt of Immunic, Joerg Neermann, a member of Life Science Partners, Vincent Ossipow, a member of Omega Funds, Jan von den Bossche, a member of Fund+, and Vital Therapies’ current president and member of the management team, Duane Nash. With the signing of the exchange agreement between the two parties, Russell J. Cox, Vital Therapies’ CEO, will be leaving the company in the near term. 

Concurrently, Vital Therapies has received commitment to raise approximately EUR26 million (USD29.62 million) in financing. The finance will be provided by Life Sciences Partners, Omega Funds, Fund+, LifeCare Partners, Bayern Kapital, High-Tech Grunderfonds and IBG Beteiligungsgesellschaft Sachsen-Anhalt  

Ladenburg Thalmann & Co. Inc. acted as exclusive financial advisor to Vital Therapies for the transaction and Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman LLP acted as legal counsel to Vital Therapies. BMO Capital Markets acted as exclusive financial advisor to Immunic for the transaction and Dentons acted as legal counsel to Immunic.

This transaction enables Vital Therapies to further advance its three next-generation programs in chronic autoimmune and inflammatory diseases and to develop new and much-needed therapies for patients with inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.

Deal History:

Update: March 27, 2019 Vital Therapies would like to thank its stockholders for their support of the proposed business combination with Immunic and remind those stockholders that have not yet voted to vote without delay “FOR” the business combination and the other proposals in the Company’s proxy statement/prospectus for the special meeting of its stockholders to be held on April 4, 2019. Vital Therapies stockholders should note that the exchange proposal (Proposal 1), the change in control proposal (Proposal 2), the name change proposal (Proposal 3) and the reverse stock split proposal (Proposal 4) must all be approved for the business combination to be completed.  If any of those proposals is not approved, the transaction will not go forward.

Announced: On January 6, 2019, Vital Therapies entered into a definitive agreement to acquire all of the outstanding shares in and Immunic, in exchange for newly issued shares in an all-stock transaction.
Deal_Rationale: This transaction enables Vital Therapies to further advance its three next-generation programs in chronic autoimmune and inflammatory diseases and to develop new and much-needed therapies for patients with inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.

Deal_Headline: Boehringer Ingelheim Acquires ViraTherapeutics for USD210 Million
Description:
Boehringer Ingelheim, a research-driven pharmaceutical company, exercises its option and acquired all shares of ViraTherapeutics, a biopharmaceutical company specializing in the development of oncolytic viral therapies. 

ViraTherapeutics developed the lead candidate VSV-GP (Vesicular Stomatitis Virus (VSV) with modified glycoprotein (GP)), which is being investigated alone and in combination with other therapies. The total transaction value of EUR210 million (USD243.7 million) is based on an option and share purchase agreement signed between the companies in August 2016. 

Oncolytic viral therapy is a cancer treatment approach with two modes of action.

Using a dual approach for potential treatment options, specifically combining immuno-oncology approaches with tumor cell-directed treatments, is central to Boehringer Ingelheim’s cancer immunology research strategy. Oncolytic virus-based therapies are consistent with and complement that strategy.

ViraTherapeutics was a portfolio company of the two venture investors EMBL Ventures and the Boehringer Ingelheim Venture Fund (BIVF). BIVF is focused on strategic investment in highly innovative biotechnology and start-up companies to help drive innovation in medical science. The BIVF has EUR250 million (USD290 million) under management and currently supervises a portfolio of 22 active companies and is one of the most active investors in immuno-oncology world-wide.

ViraTherapeutics will operate as a distinct unit of Boehringer Ingelheim’s Discovery Research organization, maintaining its innovative biotech heritage and close connections to the Medical University of Innsbruck and the regional scientific community.

This transaction enables Boehringer Ingelheim to strengthen its commitment to research and development of viral-based immuno-oncology treatment options aimed at transforming the lives of patients.
Deal_Rationale: This transaction enables Boehringer Ingelheim to strengthen its commitment to research and development of viral-based immuno-oncology treatment options aimed at transforming the lives of patients.

Financial_Advisors: Morgan Stanley  & Co LLC , BofA Securities Inc

Description:
Emergent BioSolutions Inc., has acquired Adapt Pharma Ltd, a pharmaceutical company, and its flagship product NARCAN (naloxone HCl) Nasal Spray, the needle-free formulation of naloxone approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Health Canada, for the emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose as manifested by respiratory and/or central nervous system depression. 

Total consideration for the transaction is up to USD735 million consisting of an upfront payment of USD635 million and up to USD100 million in cash for potential sales-based milestones through 2022. At the closing, the company paid USD635 million, consisting of USD60 million in Emergent common stock and USD575 million in cash, subject to customary closing adjustments, using a combination of cash-on-hand and borrowings under its new USD1.05 billion syndicated senior secured credit facilities that the company entered into to fund the transaction.

With the closing of this transaction, Emergent also acquires a development pipeline of new treatment and delivery candidates to address opioid overdose and brings on approximately 50 employees, located in the US., Canada, and Ireland, including those responsible for supply chain management, research and development, government affairs, and commercial operations.

To fund the cash portion of the acquisition, Emergent will use a combination of cash-on-hand, its existing USD200 million credit facility, and borrowings pursuant to a new USD600 million debt financing commitment provided by Wells Fargo Bank, National Association. 

This transaction will bring Adapt and Emergent together to focus on the opioid crisis, will accelerate access to NARCAN Nasal Spray through investments in public awareness and manufacturing capacity while maintaining a responsible pricing approach, and also allow Adapt to progress its R&D pipeline of additional opioid overdose and addiction treatment option.

This transaction enables Emergent BioSolutions to diversify and expand its presence within the public health threats market to respond to the opioid crisis, declared a public health emergency by the U.S. government; to further expand awareness and availability of this convenient, easy-to-administer life-saving treatment; product development pipeline with new treatment and delivery options to address opioid overdoses, and broadening Emergent BioSolutions’ portfolio of only-in-class medical countermeasures with the addition of NARCAN (R) (naloxone HCl) Nasal Spray, the only FDA-approved nasal form of naloxone indicated for the emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose.

Deal_Headline: Astellas Pharma Acquires Quethera
Description:

Deal_Headline: Sangamo Therapeutics Acquires TxCell
Legal_Advisors: Jones Day LLP
Description:
Sangamo Therapeutics Inc, a company focused on translating ground-breaking science into genomic therapies, has acquired TxCell SA, a biotechnology company, in tender offer, at a price of EUR2.58 per share in cash, for a consideration of EUR72 million (USD83.71 million).

Pursuant to the agreement, Sangamo Therapeutics, directly or through a subsidiary, has agreed that, without undue delay following the completion of the Block Transaction, it will commence a cash tender offer to acquire all of the ordinary shares of TxCell not held by Sangamo or any subsidiary of it for the offer price. In addition, Sangamo has agreed to: (a) grant to certain employees of TxCell stock options to purchase approximately 150,000 shares of Sangamo common stock, which will be granted under its existing 2018 equity incentive plan, with standard vesting conditions; and (b) enter into arrangements with holders of 495,396 “free shares” of TxCell, pursuant to which Sangamo would purchase such shares from the holders thereof from time to time through mid-2021.

The transaction enables Sangamo Therapeutics to entry into the clinic with a CAR-Treg, and intends to use its zinc finger nuclease (ZFN) gene editing technology to develop next-generation autologous and allogeneic CAR-Treg cell therapies for use in treating autoimmune diseases.

Bryan, Garnier & Co advises TxCell on this transaction.

Deal History:

Announced: On July 23, 2018, Sangamo Therapeutics entered into agreement to acquire TxCell, in tender offer, at a price of EUR2.58 per share in cash, for a consideration of EUR72 million (USD83.71 million).

Upon completion of the simplified tender offer, Sangamo would launch a squeeze-out procedure.  TxCell will be a subsidiary of Sangamo Therapeutics operating under the name Sangamo Therapeutics Therapeutics SA. Following the completion of the squeeze-out procedure, Sangamo Therapeutics intends to delist TxCell. TxCell's operations will remain based in Valbonne, France.

Deal_Headline: Ryboquin Acquires Nanogenic Solutions
Description:
Ryboquin Co Ltd, a pharmaceutical company, has acquired Nanogenic Solutions Ltd, a biotechnology company, to form a new product and platform company, which, following acquisition will be named Nanogenics Limited.

Ryboquin raised GBP4.45 million in its third funding round from new and existing share-holders to finance the deal.

The combined company is set to revolutionise gene therapy by pioneering the safe, efficacious and regular dosing of all forms of gene therapy. Currently viruses and liposomes are used in this process, which have limited applications, severe side-effects and expensive technical problems. Nanogenics Solutions is developing LipTide, an artificial virus, which acts as a custom-built delivery system that can be modified to target different cell types and deliver different payloads, making the promise of gene therapy one step closer to reality. LipTide is a protein based nanoparticle, which mimics natural viruses, but by-passes the many problems of viral delivery. The ability to regularly dose gene therapy payloads with LipTide could revolutionise the approach to gene therapy.

The transaction enables Ryboquin to form a new product and platform company, and to advance gene therapy.
Deal_Rationale: The transaction enables Ryboquin to form a new product and platform company, and to advance gene therapy.
